description: A Java UDF name may carry several OVERLOADS, resolved by the argument list at the call site: overloads differing in parameter COUNT (zero, one and two STRING arguments all under one name), overloads differing in parameter TYPE (STRING against INTEGER), and overloads with the same type but different counts. DROP FUNCTION takes a SIGNATURE and drops only that overload, leaving its siblings callable; Snowflake requires the signature, so dropping every overload means dropping each one individually. CREATE OR REPLACE likewise replaces only the matching signature and leaves the others on their old handler. A second CREATE for a signature that already exists is refused, dropping a signature that does not exist is refused while the real overload survives, and calling a name with a count no overload declares is refused. Two type-distinct overloads also resolve correctly per column inside one SELECT over a table. Converted 1:1 from udf/OverloadedFunctionTest (now retired), a JDBC test whose statements are all plain SQL; where it asserted only that a statement throws, the message it throws is pinned here.

steps.sql: SELECT greet()
SELECT greet('Alice')
SELECT greet('Bob', 'Smith')
SELECT process('test')
SELECT process(42)
DROP FUNCTION calculate(INTEGER)
SELECT calculate(10, 20)
SELECT calculate(5)
DROP FUNCTION sum_val(INTEGER)
DROP FUNCTION sum_val(INTEGER, INTEGER)
SELECT sum_val(5)
SELECT sum_val(5, 10)
SELECT multiply(5)
SELECT multiply(5, 7)
CREATE TABLE data (int_val INTEGER, str_val STRING)
INSERT INTO data VALUES (42, 'hello')
INSERT INTO data VALUES (100, 'world')
SELECT fmt_value(int_val), fmt_value(str_val) FROM data ORDER BY int_val
DROP FUNCTION sample_fn(STRING)

error.messageContains: SAMPLE_FN' does not exist or not authorized.

steps.sql: SELECT sample_fn(10)
SELECT concat_val('test')
SELECT concat_val('hello', 'world')
SELECT limited()
SELECT limited(1, 2)
